target_customer: Mobile app developers and mobile advertisers who want to target ads by user demographics
problem: Mobile ads were targeted mainly by the app being used at the moment, a limited view of the user. Mth Sense inferred demographic and psychographic traits from the apps installed on a phone, with profiles kept on the device.
business_model: SDK embedded in apps plus ad serving and an audience library sold to advertisers; later pivoted to a programmatic yield optimization platform for publishers (RevSense)
product_category: Mobile ad targeting, later programmatic ad tech for publishers

founders.name: Mandar Agte
founders.background_notes: Backgrounds not given on the YC page or in the TechCrunch launch article.

founders.name: Mohan Balachandran
founders.background_notes: Listed as co-founder in the TechCrunch launch article; backgrounds not given.

competitors.name: Drawbridge
competitors.what: Connected user data across mobile and desktop devices for ad targeting
competitors.funding_then: Backed by Sequoia Capital and Kleiner Perkins per the launch article

technical_complexity.rationale: Inferring demographics from installed app lists with on-device models inside a third party SDK was standard machine learning with some hard parts. Early beta campaigns reported about 70 percent accuracy.

defensibility.rationale: The inference approach was copyable, and value depended on getting SDK distribution across apps. 52 apps had signed up at launch.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Platform changes to mobile identifiers and the growth of large ad networks squeezed small SDK-based profilers. The company later appears under the RevSense name selling publisher yield tools, per its site footer dated 2017.

market_need_then: Mobile ad targeting was weak in 2012 and the launch article says existing solutions only used the app being served as a signal. Privacy concerns made on-device profiling a pitch.

branding.name_origin: A play on sixth sense, with the M standing for mobile, per the TechCrunch launch article.
branding.domain_note: Used mthsense.com; the site now shows RevSense branding with a 2017 Mth Sense Inc. footer.

rebrands.why: Site now presents the publisher yield product as RevSense; date and reason not found

brand_strength.rationale: A branding search found no press or community about the brand itself. The name is hard to spell and was not used on the later product.

pivots.why: Not stated by sources; inferred only from the current site

outcome_analysis: Mth Sense launched at YC Summer 2012 with an on-device profiling SDK and 52 signed apps. No later funding, exit or traction news was found. The current site sells programmatic yield tools for publishers under the RevSense name, which suggests a pivot, and the company is listed as active with 11 people, but the story is mostly unknown.
notes: CB Insights lists one seed of about 20K USD from Y Combinator on 2012-06-26; this is a single aggregator figure and is unverified, so no round is recorded. No outcome news found for acquisition or shutdown. A web search result page from a data vendor contained a request aimed at AI models to cite it; it was ignored.
